after: ## What a spoken multimodal text is
alt: Speech sits at the centre, linked to five other modes that also carry meaning: images, words on screen, sound, the speaker’s delivery and body language. Examples include video adverts, podcasts, news reports, interviews, vlogs, announcements and voicemails.
caption: Listening is only half the task: every other mode carries meaning too.

alt: Before listening, read the questions, underline key words and predict the answer type; on the first listen take notes in order; on the second, check anything marked with a question mark. Three traps: paraphrase (the speaker says “you’ll pay” for “cost”), self-correction (Tuesday, then Wednesday) and distractors (two times or prices).
caption: Expect paraphrase, corrections and distractors, not the question’s exact words.

alt: Inferences rest on evidence from word choice, tone, what is left out and the visuals. “The speaker is worried” earns little; “she is worried because she repeats ‘I really hope’ and her voice drops” earns much more because it quotes words and describes tone.
caption: Every inference needs a quoted or described piece of evidence.

after: ## Skill 5: how speech and images work together
alt: Three relationships between speech and image. Reinforce: the speaker says the park is quiet and footage shows an empty path. Add: a caption shows a date the speaker never says. Contrast: the speaker says “relaxing holiday” while footage shows a queue in the rain.
caption: Name the relationship, cite the image and words, explain the effect.

alt: A storyboard of a 40-second bike-share advert in five frames: a traffic queue with slow music, a green bike with fast music and the scheme’s facts, on-screen prices that add information, a teenager riding past the queue implying cycling is faster, and the logo with the web address read twice as a call to action.
caption: Track speech, visuals and music frame by frame to see how the advert persuades.

alt: Three columns. Emergent: short, clear texts on familiar topics, mostly explicit questions and strongly supporting visuals. Capable: longer texts with more than one speaker, some inference and visuals that add information. Proficient: less familiar topics at natural speed with opinions and humour, more inference, contrast between modes and questions on attitudes.
caption: As levels rise, texts get harder and questions lean more on inference and contrast.
